source.title: ReSAT: Training LLMs Resistant against Refusal Ablation Attacks

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates difference-in-means directions and their ablation, and reports that some safety-trained models resist rank-one ablation but remain vulnerable to joint removal of complementary directions. It therefore refines the single-direction account with results from its own interventions.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own single-direction and RSA harmful-request ASR results, training comparisons evaluated under RSA, intervention-matched MMLU results, and the stated causal effects of refreshed directions. The paper also reports selection-proxy scores and many jailbreak/utility results; these do not directly measure the claim versions and are not recorded as rows. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper extracts difference-in-means refusal directions (Arditi-style) and ablates them across layers and positions. It measures HarmBench ASR under rank-one and joint multi-direction ablation on base instruct and safety-trained checkpoints. It argues and shows that rank-one robustness does not imply subspace robustness. It also tests whether training under (cumulative) direction ablation removes the vulnerability. Its own results therefore bear on V1, V3, V4 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that single-direction robustness does not ensure safety under joint ablation of complementary directions. RSA exposes this cheaply. ReSAT lowers ASR against RSA, Geometry, SOM and several jailbreaks in key settings while preserving MMLU. Retaining direction history exposes causally active complementary directions. Add that they note over-refusal on XSTest and that gains are limited to the evaluated models and attacks.
record.recipe_differences: RSA uses the original difference-in-means candidate extraction and layer/position-wide projection idea, but adaptively selects and jointly removes complementary directions rather than testing only a single direction. The paper evaluates harmful-request ASR and utility in safety-trained checkpoints; it does not test the original direction-addition claim with generated harmless-request refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on attack rank and KL eligibility threshold. The paper reports different outcomes at KL ≤ 0.1, 0.2, and 0.5; relaxed constraints can strengthen RSA while affecting utility, with effects varying across models. Training results also vary by training recipe, cumulative versus fixed direction history, and SafeTrain round.
record.peer_reviewed: preprint; under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: Main Table 1 point estimates have no reported uncertainty. The paper provides three training seeds, but several ablation comparisons are presented as one configuration. MMLU is a limited capability measure, and the intervention-matched MMLU examples here are from one seed per model family. Some attack-selection and evaluation settings differ across methods, as the paper notes.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional RSA results for the six Llama training-ablation groups, intermediate bank effects B2–B4, direction-energy diagnostics, and other seed-level outcomes. Only the directly relevant training contrasts and B1/marginal-direction examples are retained alongside the main Single/RSA table; the remaining appendix diagnostics were omitted to keep the record focused on distinct claim-bearing results.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts. An optional probe-based addition check exists in selection, but no generated-answer result is reported.
Entirely; there is no weight-edit or abliterated-model evaluation.
Whether ordinary jailbreak attacks (GCG, PAIR, AutoDAN, etc.) work by suppressing the refusal direction. Only robustness scores are reported, not activations.
Entirely. Evaluation may transfer the first direction from the base instruct model, but no isolated transfer result is reported.
Entirely; no reasoning models are tested.

missing.what: MMLU under Single and RSA ablation for every checkpoint. Base models: Llama 67.50 clean to 64.75 Single; Mistral 60.50 to 59.50; Qwen 76.50 to 76.50. This is the capability-retention part of V1 when refusal is actually removed.
Lexical refusal rates under Single/RSA/Geometry/SOM. Needed to cross-check ASR, especially the Qwen Single column, where ASR and RR disagree (e.g. Qwen CAT Single RR 98.44 vs ASR 58.49).

RSA results at KL ≤ 0.2 and 0.5. Attack rank, ASR and MMLU change with the KL budget (e.g. Mistral ReFAT ASR 28.91 to 71.09; MMLU drops to 42.25 at KL 0.5). Multi-direction gains depend on this choice.
Ten refusal phrasings after SFT share one direction. Ablating the shared −5/L12 direction drops RR 97.11 to 2.89, while an orthogonal 'The' direction changes RR by −0.96 pp.
A fresh rank-one I-probe direction on the final ReSAT model drops RR only 100 to 97.19. It has cosine 0.79 with the initial d1.
Bank prefixes B2–B4 on M0 raise ASR 80.3–82.9 pp vs 51.2 for B1, and fall to 7.7–11.2 pp on M3.
Refresh+accumulate vs refresh+replace: 11.20% vs 29.07% rank-four ASR on M3 (paired diff 17.87 pp, 95% CI 14.13–21.87).
missing.locator: Section 5.6; Figure 3; Appendix G Panel B

missing.what: Geometry (cone) and SOM multi-direction attack ASR on all checkpoints (e.g. Mistral DeepRefusal SOM 89.94, Llama CAT Geometry 49.69 vs Single 27.34).

record.verdict_notes: Several internal inconsistencies matter for the rows. (1) The Qwen Single ASR column in Table 1 appears to use a different cohort (values are multiples of 1/159), while rank-1 RSA should reuse Single. So Qwen Single-vs-RSA ASR contrasts are unreadable; RR in Table 11 is the safer comparison. (2) Qwen Ours Single is 7.14 in Table 1 but 1.50 in Table 14. (3) The matched no-training-RSA control gives 11.20 in Table 3 but 12.00 in the text. Robustness rows for ReSAT are the study's own defense; they are kept because the training ablations bear directly on V3/V7. The direction is selected by a first-token log-odds proxy, with outcomes judged by three classifiers; Mistral runs sometimes disable the addition filter. No instructions in the text were followed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests ablation of difference-in-means directions, but does not report a generated-answer test of adding a direction to make harmless requests be refused. It does not establish that all non-refusal abilities are preserved.
The paper tests joint activation ablation and training under joint ablation, not whether ordinary jailbreak attacks work by suppressing the original single direction.
The study evaluates selected complementary directions up to rank four; it does not exhaust all possible affine, conic, or multidirectional descriptions.
No separate harmfulness-judgment versus refusal-decision test.

The protocol permits choosing a first direction from the base checkpoint or the safety-trained checkpoint, but reports no isolated transfer result across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The paper compares selected training recipes and schedules, but does not systematically identify how every training method or training stage determines whether a single removable direction exists.
